> Want a more detailed system for making dungeons? Josh McCrowell and Warren D's ENNIE- and Bloggie-winning [Designing Dungeons course](https://dungeons.hismajestytheworm.games/) is excellent.

$hoistPin: Audited every shipping sidebar against where it lands, 2026-08-08. Only the wrong ones are listed; the rest sit correctly under the section they trail. Three groups: (a) it belongs to the entry it PRECEDES, because the book prints it in the margin at the foot of the previous column — the imp/nymph desire tables, 'Why tarot?', and 'Learning the Challenge Phase' (which otherwise pins to '5. End the round', the last step of the very sequence it introduces); (b) it belongs to an ANCESTOR of the heading it fell on, because it discusses a whole section while trailing one item of it — 'Effect names' and 'Not just for Challenges' land on the single effect 'Trip', 'Sorcery' on the talent 'Dwimmercraft', 'Negative bonds' on the single bond 'Ward', 'Lyric incantations' on the Lich's 'Body', 'Initiative strategies' on 'Step 3', 'The pace of travel' on the Camp Phase's last step; (c) 'Anything that's not nailed down' is general advice on borrowing material that fell on '21. Well', an arbitrary dungeon seed. Left alone as genuinely ambiguous, your call: 'The gates' (about the outer ring, sits between the central power and the core districts — neither owns it), 'Morale' (on the Wands action 'Banter', which may well be right), 'A reminder' in ch5 (about attribute priority generally, sits between two Paths).
